title: ChatGPT Can Now Watch How You Use Your Mac
hook: A new ChatGPT feature called Computer History records your clicks and keystrokes to learn how you work — then suggests automations and picks up tasks you abandoned.
key_points: The Verge reports ChatGPT's macOS app can log your on-screen activity into a timeline.
That timeline becomes context ChatGPT and Codex can reference when you ask for something.
The pitch: it learns your workflow, suggests automations, and resumes half-done tasks.
The cost: clicks and keystrokes are among the most revealing data you produce.
Assistants that watch your whole screen need a deliberate yes, not a default on.
content_html: OpenAI has added a feature to ChatGPT's macOS app called Computer History. The Verge reports it records what you do on your computer — clicks and keystrokes — and turns that stream into a timeline the assistant can refer back to, so it can learn how you work, propose automations, and even resume tasks you left half finished.
extra_html: It's a genuine capability leap: an assistant that has seen your workflow can help in ways one that only reads your prompts cannot. It's also a different category of data. A chat log contains what you decided to share; an activity timeline contains everything else — the client names in a spreadsheet, the password manager you opened, the message you typed and deleted. Neither the usefulness nor the risk is hypothetical, which is exactly why this is a decision to make on purpose. If the automations don't solve a problem you actually have, leaving it off costs you nothing.

related.title: Your Data & Privacy
related.hook: When you type into a free AI tool, you might be the product. What you share can be stored, reviewed by humans, and used to train future models — so share like it's not private.

related.title: OpenAI Kills Its AI Browser, Bets on an Agent That Works For You
related.hook: Less than a year after launching an AI browser, OpenAI is shutting it down — and replacing the ambition behind it with 'ChatGPT Work,' an agent built to run independent tasks for hours at a time.

related.title: Can Cloud AI Be Private? Apple's Bet
related.hook: Apple's pitch for its AI is privacy: small models run on your device, and bigger ones run in the cloud — even on Google's servers — in a way Apple says gives the host no access to your data.

flashcards.prompt: What does ChatGPT's Computer History feature actually collect?
flashcards.back_html: Your activity on the Mac — clicks and keystrokes — assembled into a timeline that ChatGPT and Codex can consult when you make a request.

flashcards.prompt: Why is a keystroke-and-click timeline a bigger privacy question than a chat log?

choices.text: It captures everything you do on the machine, not just what you chose to type into the assistant
It is stored forever while chat logs are deleted instantly
It is the only AI feature that sends data over the internet

flashcards.explanation_html: A chat log holds what you deliberately shared. An activity timeline holds work you never intended to hand to an assistant at all.

flashcards.prompt: What's the sensible default for a feature like this?
flashcards.back_html: Leave it off unless the payoff is concrete for you. Broad screen-watching access deserves a deliberate decision, not a shrug at a setup prompt.
